name: Monumental Knowledge Encoding
region: Global (British Isles, Egypt, Mesoamerica, Cambodia, India, North America, Polynesia)
summary: Temples, stone circles, pyramids, and medicine wheels that encode astronomical, agricultural, and calendrical data in durable architecture — functioning as stone hard drives readable across millennia without literacy.

claims.statement: Stone circles and megalithic alignments encode solstice, equinox, and lunar cycle data with precision sufficient for agricultural calendaring, verified by archaeoastronomical survey
Mesoamerican and Southeast Asian temple complexes embed astronomical and mathematical knowledge in architectural geometry, functioning as permanent observatories and data references
Plains medicine wheels and Pacific navigational stones independently encode directional and seasonal data in non-literate cultures, demonstrating global convergence of architectural data storage

evidence.source: Ruggles (1999) Astronomy in Prehistoric Britain and Ireland, Yale University Press
Pearson et al. (2007) The Age of Stonehenge, Antiquity 81(313)
Aveni (2001) Skywatchers: A Revised and Updated Version of Skywatchers of Ancient Mexico, University of Texas Press
Mannikka (1996) Angkor Wat: Time, Space, and Kingship, University of Hawaii Press
Eddy (1974) Astronomical Alignment of the Big Horn Medicine Wheel, Science 184(4141)
Lewis (1972) We, the Navigators: The Ancient Art of Landfinding in the Pacific, University of Hawaii Press

notes: The transition from living knowledge systems to inert-material knowledge storage. Where a grove self-timestamps, a stone circle is permanent but static — it trades self-repair for extreme durability. These are not 'ceremonial' in the modern dismissive sense; they are databases in stone. Kelly (2016) argues convincingly that memory palaces and songlines are the cognitive software that runs on this architectural hardware.
